# Reloop vs the competition

> Compare Reloop with Resend, SendGrid, Mailgun, AWS SES, Postmark, Loops, and Mailchimp.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop is open-source email infrastructure (Apache 2.0): transactional API, SMTP, campaigns, webhooks, and an agent inbox. Hosted Reloop Cloud plans are Free (6,000 emails/month, 200/day), Pro $10/month (50,000), Growth $20/month (100,000), Enterprise custom. Self-host has no Reloop license fee.

## Hosted pricing (source of truth)

### What counts as an email?

Each successfully sent email counts toward your monthly quota: transactional messages, campaign sends, and SMTP relay deliveries all use credits the same way.

### Do I need a credit card to start?

No. The Free plan includes 6,000 emails per month and 200 emails per day, with no credit card required. Upgrade when your volume grows.

# Reloop vs Resend

# Reloop vs Resend

> Reloop vs Resend compared for 2026: open-source email API with self-hosting vs hosted Resend. Pricing, features, deliverability, and migration.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/resend
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/resend.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop is email infrastructure you can host or self-host (Apache 2.0, KumoMTA). Resend is a hosted DX layer over Amazon SES. Reloop Free is 6,000 emails/month (200/day); Pro is $10/month for 50,000 emails with no daily cap. Reloop is not a drop-in Resend proxy.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Pricing & Email Volume

Reloop Cloud Free is 6,000 emails/month (200/day). Pro is $10/mo for 50,000 emails with no daily cap. Overage is $0.50 vs Resend's $0.90 per 1,000. Self-hosting Reloop has no Reloop license fee (you pay your own infra).

| Feature | Reloop | Resend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free monthly emails | 6,000 / mo | 3,000 / mo |
| Daily send limit (Free tier) | 200 / day (Free also caps at 6,000 / month) | 100 / day (Free tier limited to 100 sends/day) |
| Entry paid plan | $10 / mo (50,000 emails included) | $20 / mo (50,000 emails included (no $10 tier)) |
| 100,000 emails / mo plan | $20 / mo | $35 / mo |
| Overage rate (per 1k emails) | $0.50 / 1k | $0.90 / 1k |
| Self-hosted email sends | Unlimited (Free open-source software (own infra)) | N/A (Hosted SaaS only; pay per send) |

## Sending & Receiving

Both products support sending and receiving email. Reloop runs its own MTA/MX stack (KumoMTA, Rspamd, two-way agent inbox) and is fully self-hostable, whereas Resend is a hosted DX layer over Amazon SES with webhook-oriented inbound.

| Feature | Reloop | Resend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent inbox | Yes | Yes |
| Inbox for humans | Yes | Yes |
| AI composer | Yes | Yes |
| Inbound spam scoring | Yes | - |
| REST API | Yes | Yes |
| SMTP relay | Yes | Yes |
| Official SDKs | Yes | Yes |
| React Email / HTML templates | Yes | Yes |
| Batch / broadcast sending | Yes | Yes |
| Scheduled delivery | Yes | Yes |
| A/B testing | No | No |
| MTA | Yes | No |
| Self-hostable | Yes | No |
| Open-source | Yes | No |
| Shared IPs | Yes | Yes |
| Dedicated IPs | 1 included (Growth) | Scale+ |

## Data & analytics

Core delivery telemetry overlaps. We only mark features Reloop implements in product today, with no geolocation or client fingerprinting claims.

| Feature | Reloop | Resend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delivery events | Yes | Yes |
| Bounce handling | Yes | Yes |
| Complaint / spam events | Yes | Yes |
| Open tracking | Yes | Yes |
| Click tracking | Yes | Yes |
| Unsubscribe events | Yes | Yes |
| Dashboard activity / logs | Yes | Yes |
| Geolocation on opens | Yes | No |
| Email client analytics | Yes | No |

## Reliability

This section is about control plane ownership, not a promise that Reloop is faster or more available than Resend. We do not publish third-party latency benchmarks here.

| Feature | Reloop | Resend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct MTA delivery (no SES hop) | Yes | No (Resend’s public sending path goes through Amazon SES) |
| Public status page | Yes (status.reloop.sh) | Yes |
| Self-host = your uptime domain | Yes (You operate the stack and SLOs) | No |

## Security

| Feature | Reloop | Resend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SPF | Yes | Yes |
| DKIM | Yes | Yes |
| DMARC guidance / records | Yes | Yes |
| TLS options | Yes (Domain TLS: opportunistic or enforced) | Yes |
| Webhook signature verification | Yes (HMAC-SHA256 (X-Webhook-Signature)) | Yes (Svix-style signing headers) |
| Account auth | Email OTP + OAuth (Google / GitHub) | Yes |

## Platform

| Feature | Reloop | Resend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hosted SaaS | Yes | Yes |
| Contacts / audiences | Yes (Contacts, groups, channels) | Yes (Audiences on Resend) |
| Webhook management API | Yes | Yes |
| Agent / AI inbox product | Yes | No |
| Vendor lock-in risk | Lower (Source + self-host path; still evaluate license terms) | Higher (Hosted-only proprietary stack) |

## FAQ

### Is Reloop a good Resend alternative in 2026?

Yes, if you want an open-source Resend alternative with self-hosting. Reloop matches Resend on REST API, SMTP relay, SDKs, templates, scheduled delivery, and open/click tracking, and adds an agent inbox, human inbox, AI composer, and its own MTA stack. Choose Resend if you want a hosted-only DX layer and are comfortable paying per send with no self-host path.

### How does Reloop pricing compare to Resend?

Reloop Free includes 6,000 emails per month with a 200/day cap, double Resend Free (3,000 per month, 100/day). Reloop Pro is $10/month for 50,000 emails and Growth is $20/month for 100,000 emails; Resend Pro is $20/month for 50,000 emails and $35/month for 100,000 emails. Reloop overage is $0.50 per 1,000 vs Resend $0.90 per 1,000. Self-hosted Reloop has no Reloop license fee — you pay your own infrastructure. Prices are public list prices as of October 26, 2026; see reloop.sh/pricing and resend.com/pricing.

### Is Reloop open source?

Yes. Reloop is licensed under Apache License 2.0 plus additional Reloop Labs terms: personal and internal self-host is allowed; commercial redistribution, third-party hosted services, and competing products are not. See https://reloop.sh/license. Reloop Cloud is the official hosted service.

### Is Reloop a drop-in Resend API?

No. Reloop is not a Resend proxy. Plan a small client adapter when migrating. Auth uses the x-api-key header with rl_ keys. SMTP senders only need to change host, port, and credentials.

### Does Reloop Free have a daily send limit?

Yes. Reloop Free includes 6,000 emails per month and 200 emails per day. Pro ($10/mo), Growth ($20/mo), and Enterprise have no daily cap. Self-hosted Reloop is limited by your own infrastructure, not Reloop Cloud quotas.

### How is deliverability different from Resend?

Both support SPF, DKIM, DMARC, shared and dedicated IPs, and bounce/complaint handling. The architectural difference: Reloop runs its own MTA delivery path (KumoMTA) while Resend's public sending path goes through Amazon SES. Deliverability itself still depends on domain reputation, content, and list hygiene — not the dashboard brand. Self-hosted Reloop lets you own IPs directly.

### Does Reloop support inbound email like Resend?

Yes, and it goes further. Resend offers webhook-oriented inbound receiving. Reloop adds an agent inbox with inbound spam scoring (Rspamd), a human inbox, and an AI composer — transactional, marketing, and agent email in one codebase.

### How long does migration from Resend take?

Most teams ship the swap in an afternoon: verify your domain in Reloop, swap the send client or point SMTP at Reloop with a small adapter, then re-wire delivery webhooks (Reloop uses HMAC-SHA256 X-Webhook-Signature; Resend uses Svix-style headers). Keep templates — they port directly.

### When should we stay on Resend instead of switching?

Stay on Resend if you are deeply embedded in its Audiences/broadcast workflow with no need for self-hosting, source access, inbound agent inboxes, or lower per-send overage at scale — and your volume fits comfortably in Resend's tiers. Reloop wins on ownership, platform breadth, and send-based pricing at 50k–100k+ emails per month.

# Reloop vs SendGrid

# Reloop vs SendGrid

> Reloop vs SendGrid compared for 2026: API-first open-source email with self-hosting vs Twilio bundle. Pricing, platform, and enterprise migration.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/sendgrid
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/sendgrid.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

SendGrid bundles transactional APIs, marketing campaigns, and deliverability tooling, often with annual commits. Reloop is API-first, Apache 2.0, and self-hostable, with campaigns and transactional sends in one codebase. Reloop Cloud Free is 6,000 emails/month (200/day).

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs SendGrid

| Feature | Reloop | SendGrid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open-source codebase | Yes (Apache 2.0) | No |
| Self-hostable | Yes | No |
| Transactional API | Yes | Yes |
| Marketing campaigns | Yes | Yes |
| Template editor | Yes | Yes |
| SMTP relay | Yes | Yes |
| Webhooks | Yes | Yes |
| Agent inbox | Built-in | Not included |
| Contract flexibility | Monthly tiers + self-host | Often annual enterprise |

## FAQ

### Is Reloop a good SendGrid alternative in 2026?

Yes, for teams that want a modern API-first platform without Twilio bundle pressure or annual commits. Reloop matches SendGrid on transactional API, marketing campaigns, template editor, SMTP relay, and webhooks, and adds self-hosting, an agent inbox, and monthly tiers with a self-host exit ramp. Stay on SendGrid if you are deeply embedded in subuser/IP-pool workflows with deliverability tooling your team already operates.

### How does Reloop pricing compare to SendGrid?

Reloop Pro is $10/month for 50,000 emails and Growth is $20/month for 100,000 emails, with overage at $0.50 per 1,000. SendGrid Essentials lists around $19.95/month for 50,000 emails and roughly $34.95/month at 100,000 emails — often with annual enterprise commits on top. Self-hosted Reloop has no Reloop license fee. Prices are public list prices as of September 17, 2026; verify on sendgrid.com/pricing and reloop.sh/pricing.

### Can Reloop handle SendGrid-scale volume?

Hosted Pro ($10/mo, 50,000 emails), Growth ($20/mo, 100,000 emails), and Enterprise target growing throughput; overage is $0.50 per 1,000. Self-hosted Reloop scales with your Kubernetes or bare-metal footprint.

### What about dedicated IPs?

Growth includes 1 dedicated IP and Enterprise is optional/custom. Self-hosted deployments can attach your own IPs directly to your MTA layer.

### How do templates and subusers migrate from SendGrid?

Inventory subusers, API keys, and IP pools and map each to Reloop orgs or environments. Export dynamic templates and contact segments, rebuild automations in Reloop campaigns or via API triggers, then run shadow traffic by duplicating transactional sends to Reloop in staging with real payloads before cutover.

### Does Reloop replace SendGrid marketing campaigns?

Yes. Reloop includes broadcast campaigns, templates, and contacts alongside transactional sends in one codebase — so marketing and engineering share a single template source of truth instead of a dashboard/API split.

### Is Reloop open source?

Yes. Reloop is Apache 2.0 licensed plus additional Reloop Labs terms: personal and internal self-host is allowed; commercial redistribution, third-party hosted services, and competing products are not. See https://reloop.sh/license.

### When should we stay on SendGrid?

Stay if your subuser hierarchy, IP pools, and deliverability tooling are already tuned, your annual commit pricing is favorable, and you have no need for source access, self-hosting, or agent-inbox workflows. Reloop wins on ownership, monthly flexibility, and unified transactional plus marketing sends.

# Reloop vs Mailgun

# Reloop vs Mailgun

> Reloop vs Mailgun compared for 2026: self-hostable open-source email API with agent inbox vs hosted Mailgun. Pricing, inbound, and SMTP migration.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/mailgun
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/mailgun.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop offers REST + SMTP, inbound agent inbox, and Apache 2.0 self-host. Mailgun is hosted SaaS with inbound routes. Reloop Free is 6,000 emails/month (200/day).

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Pricing & Email Volume

Mailgun prices in plan tiers: Basic at $15/mo for 10,000 emails, Foundation at $35/mo for 50,000, with overage billed from $1.30 per 1,000. Reloop Cloud Pro is $10/mo for 50,000 emails and $0.50 per 1,000 after that. Self-hosting Reloop carries no Reloop license fee; you pay your own infrastructure.

| Feature | Reloop | Mailgun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo (200 / day cap) | 100 / day (Trial period only) |
| Entry paid plan | $10 / mo (50,000 emails included) | $15 / mo (Basic · 10,000 emails) |
| 50,000 emails / mo | $10 / mo | $35 / mo (Foundation) |
| Overage rate (per 1k emails) | $0.50 / 1k | From $1.30 / 1k (Basic from $1.80 / 1k) |
| Email validation | Yes | Yes (Priced as a separate add-on) |
| Self-hosted email sends | Unlimited (Free open-source software (own infra)) | N/A (Hosted SaaS only) |

## Sending & Receiving

The sending surface overlaps closely: both speak REST and SMTP, both parse inbound mail. The split is what sits behind it. Reloop runs its own MTA and MX stack (KumoMTA, Rspamd, two-way agent inbox) and hands you the source; Mailgun is managed sending with regex-matched inbound routes.

| Feature | Reloop | Mailgun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REST API | Yes | Yes |
| SMTP relay | Yes | Yes |
| Inbound / reply handling | Agent inbox (AI triage plus webhooks) | Inbound routes (Regex match and forward) |
| Agent / AI inbox | Yes | No |
| Stored templates | Yes (React Email or HTML) | Yes (Handlebars templates) |
| Batch / broadcast sending | Yes | Yes |
| Scheduled delivery | Yes | Yes |
| Marketing campaigns | Yes | Limited (Campaign tooling is a separate Sinch product) |

## Data & Security

Delivery telemetry is comparable. We only mark what Reloop ships today, with no geolocation or client fingerprinting claims.

| Feature | Reloop | Mailgun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delivery events | Yes | Yes |
| Bounce & complaint handling | Yes | Yes |
| Open & click tracking | Yes | Yes |
| Suppression lists | Yes | Yes |
| Dashboard activity / logs | Yes | Yes |
| Webhook signature verification | Yes (HMAC-SHA256 (X-Webhook-Signature)) | Yes (HMAC with account signing key) |
| SPF / DKIM / DMARC | Yes | Yes |

## Ownership & Exit

This is the section that decides most Mailgun migrations. Mailgun is hosted-only under Sinch, so leaving means rebuilding on someone else's stack. Reloop ships the source and a self-host path, so the exit is a deployment target rather than a rewrite.

| Feature | Reloop | Mailgun |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open-source codebase | Yes (Apache 2.0 plus Reloop Labs terms) | No |
| Self-hostable | Yes | No |
| Direct MTA control | Yes (KumoMTA under your control) | No (Managed sending only) |
| Dedicated IPs | 1 included (Growth plan; bring your own when self-hosted) | Paid add-on (Plan-tiered availability) |
| Vendor lock-in risk | Lower (Source plus self-host path; still evaluate license terms) | Higher (Hosted-only proprietary stack) |

## FAQ

### Is Reloop a good Mailgun alternative in 2026?

Yes, for teams that want the same REST + SMTP sending surface with source access and a self-host path. Reloop adds an agent inbox with spam scoring and threading, campaigns beyond pure transactional sends, and send-based pricing ($10/month for 50,000 emails vs Mailgun Foundation $35/month). Stay on Mailgun if inbound routes and Sinch-bundled tooling already fit and volume sits comfortably in your current tier.

### Can Reloop replace Mailgun inbound routes?

Reloop's agent inbox and webhook model cover reply handling and automated triage. Map your existing inbound URLs to Reloop handlers during migration.

### Do we lose deliverability moving off Mailgun?

Deliverability depends on domain reputation, content, and IPs, not the dashboard brand. Self-hosted Reloop lets you own IPs directly; hosted Reloop manages shared pools like other providers.

### How does Reloop Cloud pricing compare to Mailgun?

Mailgun Basic is $15/month for 10,000 emails and Foundation is $35/month for 50,000, with overage from $1.30 per 1,000. Reloop Pro is $10/month for 50,000 emails and Growth is $20/month for 100,000, with overage at $0.50 per 1,000. Self-hosted Reloop has no Reloop license fee; you pay your own infrastructure. Prices are public list prices as of September 17, 2026.

### Do SMTP senders need code changes?

No. Applications sending over SMTP change host, port, and credentials only. API senders need a small client adapter, since Reloop is not a drop-in Mailgun proxy.

### How do Mailgun validation and dedicated IPs map to Reloop?

Mailgun prices validation and dedicated IPs as add-ons above Foundation tiers. Reloop includes validation in-platform and Growth includes 1 dedicated IP; self-hosted deployments attach your own IPs directly to the MTA layer — so compare the all-in bill, not just the base tier.

### How long does migration from Mailgun take?

SMTP senders cut over in minutes (host, port, credentials) while both providers stay live during DKIM/SPF propagation. API senders need a small adapter plus inbound-route remapping and suppression-list import — most teams finish domain by domain in an afternoon.

### Is Reloop open source?

Yes. Reloop is Apache 2.0 licensed plus additional Reloop Labs terms: personal and internal self-host is allowed; commercial redistribution, third-party hosted services, and competing products are not. See https://reloop.sh/license.

# Reloop vs AWS SES

> Learn how Reloop compares to Amazon SES as an email platform, not just an SMTP pipe.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/aws-ses
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/aws-ses.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

SES is raw sending infrastructure. Reloop is a full email platform (API, campaigns, dashboard, agent inbox) that you can host or self-host. SES is often cheaper at extreme volume; Reloop competes on platform TCO, not on being the cheapest SMTP pipe.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs AWS SES

| Feature | Reloop | AWS SES |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open-source platform | Yes (Apache 2.0) | No |
| Self-host on your AWS account | Yes | SES only |
| Marketing campaigns UI | Yes | No (DIY) |
| Transactional API | Yes | Yes |
| Built-in delivery dashboard | Yes | CloudWatch / DIY |
| Webhooks | Native | SNS configuration |
| Template management | Yes | Limited |
| Agent inbox | Yes | No |
| Per-email list price | Tier bundles | Very low at scale |

## FAQ

### Is Reloop cheaper than SES at 10M emails/month?

SES raw sending is often cheaper at extreme volume. Reloop competes on platform TCO (engineering time, campaign tooling, support, and unified ops), not on being the cheapest SMTP pipe.

### Can we migrate boto3 sends to Reloop?

Yes. Replace AWS SDK send calls with Reloop REST or SMTP. Map SNS bounce notifications to Reloop webhook endpoints.

### Do we need both SES and Reloop?

Not usually. Self-hosted Reloop includes outbound delivery. Some teams keep SES as an MTA backend during transition, but that is an advanced integration, not the default path.

# Reloop vs Loops

> Compare Reloop to Loops: send-based pricing vs contact-list pricing, plus transactional API and self-host.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/loops
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/loops.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Loops prices by contact list size. Reloop prices by emails sent. Reloop Free is 6,000 emails/month (200/day); Pro is $10/month for 50,000 emails; Growth is $20/month for 100,000 emails. Reloop is the ESP/MTA, not a lifecycle UI on top of another sender.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Pricing & Economic Model

Loops charges based on your contact list size, penalizing list growth even for inactive subscribers. Reloop charges purely for emails sent (or $0 when self-hosted), ensuring your bill scales with activity, not database size.

| Feature | Reloop | Loops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pricing basis | Emails sent (Pay for actual volume used) | Contact list size (Bill increases as list grows) |
| Free monthly tier | 6,000 emails / mo (200 / day cap) | 1,000 contacts |
| Entry paid plan | $10 / mo (50,000 emails included) | $49 / mo (10k contacts) |
| 100,000 volume plan | $20 / mo | $399 / mo (100k contacts) |
| Self-hosted email sends | Unlimited ($0) (Free open-source engine (own infra)) | N/A (Closed SaaS only) |

## Unified Infrastructure & Sending

Loops is designed for product onboarding loops, forcing teams to buy a separate vendor (Resend or Postmark) for transactional emails. Reloop handles transactional API sends, marketing broadcasts, and AI agent inboxes under one unified platform.

| Feature | Reloop | Loops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transactional REST API | Yes | Limited (Basic event triggers only) |
| SMTP relay | Yes | No (No raw SMTP interface) |
| Lifecycle & onboarding campaigns | Yes | Yes (Core focus) |
| Broadcast / marketing newsletters | Yes | Yes |
| Agent / AI inbound inbox | Yes | No |
| React Email / HTML templates | Yes | HTML / Visual editor |
| Open-source MTA engine | Yes (KumoMTA) | No (Proprietary) |
| Self-hostable | Yes | No |

## Deliverability & Data Ownership

Reloop owns its delivery engine and allows full data sovereignty, whereas Loops routes through third-party email infrastructure.

| Feature | Reloop | Loops |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct MTA control | Yes (KumoMTA) | No (Relies on third-party senders) |
| Domain TLS enforcement | Yes | Yes |
| Webhook signature verification | Yes (HMAC-SHA256) | Yes |
| Single sender reputation pool | Yes (Transactional + Marketing unified) | Split (Requires 2nd vendor for transactional) |
| Data export & sovereignty | Full control (Self-host or export anytime) | CSV export |

## FAQ

### Why should we choose send-based pricing over contact-based pricing?

Contact-based pricing charges you for inactive leads and users who never open your emails. Reloop's send-based pricing charges for emails sent. Free is 6,000 emails/month (200/day); paid overage is $0.50 per 1,000.

### Can Reloop handle both marketing campaigns and transactional APIs?

Yes. Reloop includes transactional API endpoints, SMTP relay, templates, broadcast campaigns, and an agent inbox. Reloop is the email infrastructure, not a connector to another ESP.

### Can we self-host Reloop while migrating from Loops?

Yes. Reloop is Apache 2.0. You can deploy on your own Kubernetes or Docker infrastructure with no Reloop license fee. You still pay for your own servers and IPs.

# Reloop vs AgentMail

> Reloop vs AgentMail for AI agent inboxes: pricing, inbox limits, threads and replies, IMAP, MCP, webhooks, custom domains, self-hosting, and which one fits your agent.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/agentmail
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/agentmail.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs AgentMail for AI agent inboxes: pricing, inbox limits, threads and replies, IMAP, MCP, webhooks, custom domains, self-hosting, and which one fits your agent.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs AgentMail

| Feature | Reloop | AgentMail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Focus | Full email platform with agent inboxes | Inboxes for AI agents |
| Free tier | 6,000 emails / mo, 200 / day, 3 inboxes | 3,000 emails / mo, 100 / day, 3 inboxes |
| First paid plan | $10 / mo: 50,000 emails, 5 inboxes | $20 / mo: 10,000 emails, 10 inboxes |
| Next plan | $20 / mo: 100,000 emails, 10 inboxes, dedicated IP | $200 / mo: 150 inboxes, 15,000 emails / day |
| Instant address without a domain | No (needs a verified domain) | Yes (@agentmail.to) |
| Threads and reply in thread | Yes | Yes |
| IMAP access | Yes | Yes |
| Hosted MCP server | Yes | Yes |
| Real-time events | Webhooks | Webhooks and WebSockets |
| Transactional sending API | Yes | Sends from inboxes |
| Campaigns and automations | Yes | No |
| Open source | Yes (Apache 2.0) | SDKs only (MIT) |
| Self-host | Yes, unlimited inboxes | No |

## FAQ

### Is Reloop an open-source AgentMail alternative?

Yes. Reloop is Apache 2.0 and includes agent inboxes with threads, replies, IMAP and an MCP server. You can use Reloop Cloud or self-host it with no inbox limits.

### Can I get an inbox without owning a domain?

On AgentMail, yes: inboxes default to an @agentmail.to address. Reloop mailboxes live on a domain you've verified, so your agent sends as your brand.

### How many inboxes can I create?

AgentMail: 3 free, 10 on Developer ($20), 150 on Startup ($200), plus $2 per extra inbox. Reloop Cloud: 3 free, 5 on Pro ($10), 10 on Growth ($20), and unlimited when self-hosted.

### Can a human and an agent share the same inbox?

Yes, on both. Open the inbox over IMAP in any mail client while the agent uses the API or MCP server on the same threads.

### Does Reloop work with Claude, Cursor and ChatGPT?

Yes. Add https://reloop.sh/mcp as an MCP server and sign in. See the MCP server docs, or build your own agent with our guide to an AI agent that reads and replies to email.

# Reloop vs Brevo

> Reloop vs Brevo compared honestly: pricing by email volume, the transactional API, campaigns and automations, inbound and agent inboxes, deliverability, self-hosting, and how to switch.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/brevo
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/brevo.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs Brevo compared honestly: pricing by email volume, the transactional API, campaigns and automations, inbound and agent inboxes, deliverability, self-hosting, and how to switch.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Brevo

| Feature | Reloop | Brevo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | 300 / day |
| Entry paid plan | $10 for 50,000 emails | Starter from $9 for 5,000 emails |
| Plan with automations | Every plan | Standard and up (from $18) |
| Priced by | Emails sent | Emails sent |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | Higher tiers only |
| Open source | Yes (Apache 2.0) | No |

| Agent inbox | Yes | No |
| SMS and WhatsApp | No | Yes |
| CRM and live chat | No | Yes |
| SMTP relay | Yes | Yes |

## FAQ

### Is Brevo the same as Sendinblue?

Yes. Sendinblue rebranded to Brevo in 2023. The API moved to api.brevo.com, but the product is the same.

### Is Reloop cheaper than Brevo?

For most sending volumes, yes. Brevo's Starter plan begins at $9 for 5,000 emails a month; Reloop's Pro plan is $10 for 50,000. Brevo's free plan allows more mail per day (300 vs 100).

### Can Reloop replace Brevo's marketing features?

Partly. Reloop covers contacts, groups, subscription channels, broadcast campaigns and event-driven automations. It does not do SMS, WhatsApp, live chat, landing pages or a sales CRM.

### Does Brevo support self-hosting?

No. Brevo is a hosted service only. Reloop can run on your own server under the Apache 2.0 license.

### Which has better deliverability?

For most senders, neither will be the deciding factor. Your SPF, DKIM and DMARC setup and list quality matter far more. Start with our authentication guide.

Path: /compare/cloudflare-email

# Reloop vs Cloudflare Email Service

> Reloop vs Cloudflare Email Service compared: pricing at 3k to 250k emails a month, the Workers binding vs an HTTP API, DNS requirements, events, inbound email, marketing mail and lock-in.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/cloudflare-email
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/cloudflare-email.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs Cloudflare Email Service compared: pricing at 3k to 250k emails a month, the Workers binding vs an HTTP API, DNS requirements, events, inbound email, marketing mail and lock-in.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Cloudflare Email Service

| Feature | Reloop | Cloudflare Email Service |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Status | Generally available | Sending in public beta, Routing GA |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | Sending to your own verified addresses only |
| Paid entry point | $10 / mo for 50k | Workers Paid ($5 / mo minimum), 3,000 emails included |
| Price per extra 1,000 | $0.50 | $0.35 |
| Domain DNS | Any DNS provider | Must use Cloudflare DNS |
| Marketing email | Yes (campaigns) | No, transactional only |
| Templates | Yes, {{{variables}}} | Not documented |
| Contacts, campaigns, automations | Yes | No |
| Events | Signed HTTP webhooks | Cloudflare Queues |
| Inbound email | Stored mailboxes, API, MCP, IMAP | Email Routing to addresses or Workers |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | Not documented |
| Open source / self-host | Yes (Apache 2.0) | No |

## FAQ

### Is Cloudflare Email Service free?

Inbound Email Routing is free and unlimited. Sending to arbitrary recipients requires the Workers Paid plan ($5 a month minimum), which includes 3,000 emails a month, then $0.35 per 1,000. On the free plan you can only send to destination addresses verified in your account.

### Can I use Cloudflare Email Service without Cloudflare DNS?

No. Cloudflare's docs say you must be using Cloudflare DNS to use Email Service. Reloop works with any DNS provider.

### Can I send newsletters with Cloudflare Email Service?

No. Cloudflare says Email Service supports transactional email only. Reloop supports both transactional email and marketing campaigns.

### Can I use Reloop from Cloudflare Workers?

Yes. Call the HTTP API with fetch, or use the reloop-email SDK with the nodejs_compat flag. Our Workers guide covers secrets, waitUntil, retries and Queues.

### Which is cheaper?

Reloop below roughly 200,000 emails a month ($10 for 50k, $20 for 100k). Cloudflare above that, because $0.35 per 1,000 is lower than our $0.50 overage. Self-hosted Reloop has no per-email cost.

# Reloop vs Customer.io

> Reloop vs Customer.io compared honestly: per-email vs per-profile pricing at 10k to 100k profiles, journeys vs automations, transactional API and SMTP, inbound inboxes, self-hosting, plus how to switch.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/customer-io
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/customer-io.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs Customer.io compared honestly: per-email vs per-profile pricing at 10k to 100k profiles, journeys vs automations, transactional API and SMTP, inbound inboxes, self-hosting, plus how to switch.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Customer.io

| Feature | Reloop | Customer.io |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pricing basis | Emails sent | Profiles stored (people and objects) |
| Free tier | 6,000 emails / mo, 200 / day | No free plan on the pricing page |
| Entry paid plan | $10 / mo (50,000 emails) | $100 / mo (5,000 profiles, 1M emails) |
| Extra volume | $0.50 per 1,000 emails | $0.009 per extra profile, $0.12 per 1,000 extra emails |
| Next plan | $20 / mo (100,000 emails, dedicated IP) | Premium, from $1,000 / mo billed annually |
| Channels | Email | Email, push, in-app, SMS (SMS priced separately) |
| Event-triggered automations | Yes | Yes (Journeys) |
| Transactional API | Yes | Yes |
| SMTP relay | Yes | No |
| Inbound email / agent inbox | Yes | No |
| Template language | {{{variables}}} | Liquid |
| Open source / self-host | Yes (Apache 2.0) | No |

## FAQ

### Why is Customer.io more expensive than Reloop?

Customer.io is priced by profiles stored, starting at $100 a month for 5,000 profiles, plus $0.009 for each extra profile. Reloop is priced by emails sent: $10 for 50,000 and $20 for 100,000, whatever the size of your list.

### Can Reloop replace Customer.io?

For email, yes: event-triggered automations, broadcasts, transactional sends and SMTP. If your journeys also use push, in-app messages or SMS, Reloop doesn't cover those channels.

### Does Customer.io have a free plan?

No free plan is listed on its pricing page; paid plans start at $100 a month. Reloop's free tier sends 6,000 emails a month with no limit on contacts.

### Do Liquid templates work in Reloop?

Not directly. Reloop substitutes {{{variable}}} placeholders. Simple Liquid variables convert one-to-one; loops and filters should be rendered in your code, or with React Email, before you send.

### Can I self-host Customer.io?

No. Customer.io is a hosted service. Reloop is Apache 2.0 and can run on your own server with the same API.

Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/elastic-email.md

Reloop vs Elastic Email compared: Email API and Email Marketing plans, pricing at 3k to 250k emails a month, developer experience, inbound mail, dedicated IPs, self-hosting, and how to switch.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Elastic Email

| Feature | Reloop | Elastic Email |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | 3,000 / mo, 100 / day |
| 50,000 emails / mo | $10 | $19 (Starter) or $49 (Pro) |
| 100,000 emails / mo | $20 | Set by a volume slider |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | Add-on: $40/mo on Starter, $50/mo on Pro |

## FAQ

### Is Reloop cheaper than Elastic Email?

At 50,000 emails a month, yes: $10 on Reloop vs $19 on Elastic Email's Starter API plan, or $49 if you need webhooks and inbound. At millions of emails a month, Elastic Email's volume pricing may be lower, so compare at your real volume.

### Do both have a free plan?

Yes. Reloop's free tier is 6,000 emails a month, capped at 200 a day. Elastic Email's free API plan is 3,000 a month, capped at 100 a day, and keeps logs for 3 days.

### Does Elastic Email support inbound email?

Yes, inbound email processing is part of its Pro API plan ($49/mo). Reloop receives mail on every plan into stored, threaded mailboxes you can read over the API, MCP or IMAP.

Yes. Use smtp.reloop.sh on port 587 with STARTTLS, and your API key as both the username and the password.

### Is Elastic Email open source?

No. Elastic Email is a hosted service. Reloop is open source under Apache 2.0 and can run on your own server.

# Reloop vs Lettermint

> Reloop vs Lettermint compared honestly: pricing at real volumes, EU hosting and jurisdiction, the send API, broadcasts, inbound mail and agent inboxes, deliverability, self-hosting, and how to switch.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/lettermint
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/lettermint.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs Lettermint compared honestly: pricing at real volumes, EU hosting and jurisdiction, the send API, broadcasts, inbound mail and agent inboxes, deliverability, self-hosting, and how to switch.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Lettermint

| Feature | Reloop | Lettermint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Company | Reloop Labs | Lettermint B.V. (Netherlands) |
| Where email data lives | Self-host: your server. Cloud: Hetzner, with EU data centers | EU (UpCloud in the Netherlands, backups on OVHcloud in Germany) |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | 300 / mo, no daily limit |
| 50,000 emails / mo | $10 | €40 (Starter) / €45 (Growth) / €55 (Pro) |
| Overage | $0.50 per 1,000 | €1.10 to €1.50 per 1,000 at the 10k–50k tiers |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | €50 / mo add-on, Pro at 300k+ |
| Inbound email | Mailboxes with threads, API, MCP, IMAP | Parsed and posted to a signed webhook (Starter and up) |
| Contacts, campaigns, automations | Yes, every plan | Broadcast sending route; no contacts or automations in its docs |
| Open source | Yes (Apache 2.0) | SDKs only; the platform is proprietary |
| Self-host | Yes | No |
| ISO 27001 | Not published | ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified |
| SMTP relay | Yes | Yes |

## FAQ

### Is Reloop cheaper than Lettermint?

For most volumes, yes. At 50,000 emails a month Reloop is $10 and Lettermint is €40 on Starter. Reloop's free tier is also bigger: 6,000 a month vs 300. Around a million emails a month the two get close, so price your real volume.

### Where does Lettermint store data?

In the EU. Its sub-processor list names UpCloud in the Netherlands for hosting and OVHcloud in Germany for encrypted backups. Lettermint B.V. is a Dutch company, and its DPA is governed by Dutch law.

### Does Reloop have an EU region?

Yes. Reloop Cloud runs on Hetzner, with EU data centers. It comes with a DPA based on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and a public sub-processor list. If you want full control over where data lives, you can also self-host Reloop on your own EU server; it's the same open-source code.

### Does Lettermint support inbound email?

Yes, on Starter and up. It parses incoming mail and posts it to your endpoint as a signed webhook. Reloop stores incoming mail in threaded mailboxes you can read and reply to over the API, MCP or IMAP.

### Can Lettermint send newsletters?

Yes, through a separate broadcast route with its own sending infrastructure and automatic unsubscribe handling. You manage the list and content yourself. Reloop also has contacts, campaigns and automations.

### Can I self-host Lettermint?

No. Lettermint is a hosted service; only its SDKs are open source. Reloop is open source under Apache 2.0 and runs on your own server with the same API.

# Reloop vs Listmonk

Reloop vs Listmonk compared honestly: what each one is, sending infrastructure, newsletters vs transactional mail, automations, inboxes, resource use and licensing, plus how to switch or run them together.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Listmonk

| Feature | Reloop | Listmonk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | Email infrastructure: API, SMTP relay, campaigns, automations, inboxes | Newsletter and mailing list manager |
| License | Apache 2.0 | AGPLv3 |
| Hosted option | Yes (Reloop Cloud) | No, self-host only |
| Sends mail itself | Yes, own MTA (KumoMTA) | No, needs an external SMTP server |
| Stack | Bun services, Postgres, KumoMTA | Single Go binary + Postgres |
| Transactional API | Yes | Yes (POST /api/tx, template-based) |
| Campaigns / newsletters | Yes | Yes, its core strength |
| Event-triggered automations | Yes | No drip sequences |
| Inbound email / inboxes | Yes, with threads, API, MCP and IMAP | No |
| Bounce handling | Built into the MTA | POP3 bounce mailbox or provider webhooks |

## FAQ

### Is Listmonk an alternative to Reloop?

Partly. Listmonk replaces Reloop's newsletter and campaign features, but not the sending infrastructure, automations or inboxes. It needs an external SMTP server to deliver mail, which can be Reloop.

### Can Listmonk send through Reloop?

Yes. Add smtp.reloop.sh on port 587 (STARTTLS) as an SMTP server in Listmonk's settings, with your Reloop API key as both username and password.

### Does Listmonk support drip campaigns or automations?

Not built in. Listmonk focuses on lists and campaigns; teams that need sequences usually connect its transactional API to an external workflow tool. Reloop has event-triggered automations with delays and conditions.

### Which is lighter to self-host?

Listmonk. It's a single Go binary plus Postgres and runs comfortably on a tiny server. Reloop includes an MTA, inbound mail and spam scoring, so its documented minimum is 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of RAM.

### What licenses do they use?

Listmonk is AGPLv3. Reloop is Apache 2.0. Both are free to self-host.

## FAQ

### Is Reloop cheaper than MailerSend?

Yes, at every paid volume we compared. 50,000 emails a month is $10 on Reloop and $35 on MailerSend Starter; 100,000 is $20 vs $68. Reloop's free tier is also larger: 6,000 emails a month vs 500.

### Does MailerSend have a free plan?

Yes. It includes 500 emails a month, 1 domain, 1 template, 1 webhook and 100 API requests a day. Paid plans start with Hobby at $7 a month for 5,000 emails.

### Can I keep my MailerSend templates?

The HTML moves over as-is. Change {{variable}} placeholders to {{{variable}}}, save the template in Reloop, and send it by ID.

### Does MailerSend support self-hosting?

No. MailerSend is hosted-only. Reloop can run on your own server under the Apache 2.0 license.

### Which is better for receiving email?

MailerSend forwards parsed inbound mail to a webhook or address and counts each forward against your quota. Reloop stores it in threaded mailboxes you can read and reply to over the API, MCP or IMAP, which suits support inboxes and AI agents.

| Feature | Reloop | MailPace |

### Where does MailPace host data?

Its DPA says stored data is hosted in France and stays in the EU, except that outgoing mail is sent through SMTP servers in the UK. MailPace itself is a UK company, OhMySMTP Ltd.

# Reloop vs Mandrill

> Reloop vs Mandrill (Mailchimp Transactional) for developers: block pricing and the required Mailchimp plan, API and templates, webhooks, inbound, dedicated IPs, and how to migrate.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/mandrill
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/mandrill.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs Mandrill (Mailchimp Transactional) for developers: block pricing and the required Mailchimp plan, API and templates, webhooks, inbound, dedicated IPs, and how to migrate.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Mandrill

| Feature | Reloop | Mandrill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Buy on its own | Yes | No: add-on to Mailchimp Standard or Premium |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | Up to 500 trial sends to a verified domain |
| Billing unit | Monthly plan + $0.50 per 1,000 over | Blocks of 25,000 emails |
| 50,000 emails / mo | $10 | $40 in blocks + Mailchimp plan |
| 100,000 emails / mo | $20 | $80 in blocks + Mailchimp plan |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | $29.95 / mo add-on |
| Templates | {{{variables}}}, visual editor | Merge tags `*\ |
| Webhook signing | HMAC-SHA256, Reloop-Signature | HMAC-SHA1, X-Mandrill-Signature |
| Inbound email | Mailboxes with threads, API, MCP, IMAP | Routes posted to your webhook |
| SMTP relay | Yes | Yes |

## FAQ

### Can I use Mandrill without a paid Mailchimp plan?

No. Mailchimp Transactional is an add-on to the Standard or Premium Marketing plans (or the legacy Monthly Plan). The Essentials plan isn't eligible. New users get up to 500 trial sends to a verified domain.

### How much does Mandrill cost for 100,000 emails?

Four blocks of 25,000 at $20 each, so $80 a month, plus your Mailchimp Standard or Premium plan. On Reloop, 100,000 emails a month is $20 on Growth, with a dedicated IP included.

### Do my Mandrill Handlebars templates work in Reloop?

Simple variables do, once you switch them to triple braces: {{{first_name}}}. Conditionals and loops don't; resolve them in your code and pass the result in as a variable.

### Is there a free Mandrill plan?

There's no ongoing free tier, only up to 500 trial sends. Reloop's free tier is 6,000 emails a month with a 200-a-day cap.

### Does Reloop support SMTP like Mandrill?

Yes. Use smtp.reloop.sh on port 587 with STARTTLS, with your API key as both the username and password.

# Reloop vs Plunk

> Reloop vs Plunk, two open-source email platforms compared: hosted pricing, licenses, self-hosting requirements, sending infrastructure, inbound email and automations, plus how to switch.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/plunk
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/plunk.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs Plunk, two open-source email platforms compared: hosted pricing, licenses, self-hosting requirements, sending infrastructure, inbound email and automations, plus how to switch.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Plunk

| Feature | Reloop | Plunk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| License | Apache 2.0 | AGPL-3.0 |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | 1,000 / mo, with Plunk branding |
| Paid pricing | Plans: $10 for 50k, $20 for 100k | $0.001 per email, no base fee |
| 50,000 emails / mo | $10 | about $50 |
| 100,000 emails / mo | $20 | about $100 |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | Not offered on the hosted plan |

## FAQ

### Are Reloop and Plunk both open source?

Yes. Reloop is Apache 2.0 and Plunk is AGPL-3.0. Both can be self-hosted with Docker. The main practical difference is that AGPL requires you to share modifications if you offer a modified version over a network.

### Does self-hosted Plunk need AWS?

Yes. Plunk's self-hosting guide requires an AWS SES account for sending, along with PostgreSQL and Redis. Self-hosted Reloop sends through its own MTA, so no AWS account is needed.

### Which is cheaper on the hosted plans?

It depends on volume. Plunk charges $0.001 per email with no base fee, so it's cheap for tiny or irregular volumes. From around 10,000 emails a month, Reloop's plans cost less: $10 for 50k and $20 for 100k.

### Can both receive email?

Yes. Plunk processes inbound mail with routing rules. Reloop stores it in threaded mailboxes you can read over the API, MCP or IMAP, and reply to in one call.

### Do my Plunk templates work in Reloop?

The HTML does. Change the placeholders from {{ firstName }} to {{{first_name}}} and pass the values as template variables.

Reloop vs Postal compared honestly: two open-source, self-hosted email platforms. Architecture, requirements, sending API, inbound mail, webhooks, marketing features and when each one is the right pick.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs Postal

| Feature | Reloop | Postal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| License | Apache 2.0 | MIT |
| Language | TypeScript (Bun) | Ruby |
| Hosted option | Yes (free tier, from $10/mo) | No, self-host only |
| Self-host | Yes, one-command installer | Yes, Docker + CLI |
| Sending engine | KumoMTA | Postal's own MTA |

## FAQ

### Are both Reloop and Postal free and open source?

Yes. Postal is MIT-licensed and Reloop is Apache 2.0. Both are free to run on your own server. Reloop also has a hosted service with a free tier of 6,000 emails a month and paid plans from $10 for 50k.

### Does Postal have a hosted version?

Postal doesn't offer an official hosted service. You run it on your own infrastructure.

### Which is lighter to run?

Postal. It's a focused mail server and its documented minimum is 2 CPU cores, 4 GB of RAM and 25 GB of disk. Reloop's minimum is similar on CPU and RAM but needs about 35 GB of disk, because it ships inboxes, campaigns, automations and the dashboard alongside the MTA.

### Can Postal store inbound mail in mailboxes?

Postal forwards inbound mail to an HTTP endpoint, an SMTP server or an email address. Storing and threading it is up to your application. Reloop stores inbound mail in threaded mailboxes you can read over the API, IMAP or MCP.

### Can I use Postal's SMTP settings with Reloop?

Yes, with new credentials. Point your SMTP client at your Reloop host (smtp.reloop.sh on hosted) and use your Reloop API key as both the username and password.

# Reloop vs SMTP2GO

> Reloop vs SMTP2GO compared honestly: SMTP relay setup for WordPress, apps and devices, pricing at 3k to 250k emails a month, API, webhooks, dedicated IPs, inbound and self-hosting, plus how to switch.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/smtp2go
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/smtp2go.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs SMTP2GO compared honestly: SMTP relay setup for WordPress, apps and devices, pricing at 3k to 250k emails a month, API, webhooks, dedicated IPs, inbound and self-hosting, plus how to switch.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs SMTP2GO

| Feature | Reloop | SMTP2GO |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | 1,000 / mo |
| 10,000 emails / mo | $10 | $10 |
| 100,000 emails / mo | $20 | $75 |
| Overage per 1,000 | $0.50 | $1 (Starter), $0.85 (Professional) |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | Included on Professional ($75) |
| SMTP relay | Yes, port 587 (STARTTLS) | Yes, many ports incl. 2525, 8025, 80, 465, 443 |
| HTTP API | Yes, with official SDKs | Yes |
| Webhooks | Yes, signed (HMAC) | Yes |
| Inbound email | Mailboxes with threads, API, MCP, IMAP | Not a focus |
| Campaigns and automations | Yes | No |
| SMS | No | Yes |
| Open source / self-host | Yes (Apache 2.0) | No |

## FAQ

### Can I use Reloop as an SMTP relay for WordPress?

Yes. Install any SMTP plugin and set host smtp.reloop.sh, port 587, TLS/STARTTLS, and your Reloop API key as both the username and password. The From address must be on a domain you've verified in Reloop.

### Which ports does Reloop's SMTP relay support?

Port 587 with STARTTLS. Implicit TLS on 465 isn't supported, so leave "SSL" or secure: true off. If your network blocks 587, SMTP2GO's alternate ports are an advantage; with Reloop, send over the HTTPS API instead.

### Is Reloop cheaper than SMTP2GO?

At 10,000 emails they're the same ($10). Above that Reloop is cheaper: $10 vs about $50 at 50k, and $20 vs $75 at 100k. Below 6,000 a month Reloop's free tier covers you if you stay under 200 a day.

### Does SMTP2GO offer a dedicated IP?

Yes, on the Professional plan ($75 a month for 100,000 emails) and above. Reloop includes one on Growth ($20 a month for 100,000 emails).

### Can I self-host Reloop as my own SMTP relay?

Yes. Reloop is Apache 2.0 and includes the SMTP relay. Run it on your own server and point your apps at your own SMTP host. You'll own IP reputation and warm-up, so most teams start hosted.

| Log retention | 45 days | 7 to 90 days, by plan |
| Open source | Yes (Apache 2.0) | No |
| Self-host | Yes | No |
| SMTP relay | Yes | Yes |

## FAQ

### Is Reloop cheaper than Sweego?

At low volume Reloop's free tier goes further (200 emails a day vs 100), and both entry plans are around 10 (dollars for Reloop, euros for Sweego). At 100,000 emails a month Reloop is $20 with a dedicated IP, while Sweego Startup starts at €79.

### Does Reloop send SMS?

No. Reloop is email only. If you need SMS, Sweego sends both from one account, and you can use Sweego for SMS alongside Reloop for email.

### Where does Sweego host data?

In France. Sweego says it runs on OVHcloud (Gravelines) and Scaleway (DC5), and that data is never sent outside the European Union. It is operated by Mindbaz, a French company based in Lille.

### Does Reloop Cloud have an EU region?

Yes. Reloop Cloud runs on Hetzner, with EU data centers, and comes with a DPA based on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. If you want full control over location, you can also self-host Reloop on your own EU server.

### Can Sweego receive email?

Yes, on paid plans. Sweego posts each incoming message to your webhook as JSON. Reloop stores incoming mail in threaded mailboxes you can read and reply to over the API, MCP or IMAP.

### Can I self-host Sweego?

No. Sweego is a hosted service. Reloop is open source under Apache 2.0 and runs on your own server with the same API.

- Compare index: https://reloop.sh/compare.md
- License (Apache 2.0): https://reloop.sh/license

# Reloop vs useSend

> Reloop vs useSend compared honestly: license, hosted pricing at 3k to 1M emails, self-hosting with and without AWS SES, API and webhooks, inbound mail, and how to switch.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/usesend
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/compare/usesend.md
Canonical pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

Reloop vs useSend compared honestly: license, hosted pricing at 3k to 1M emails, self-hosting with and without AWS SES, API and webhooks, inbound mail, and how to switch.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs useSend

| Feature | Reloop | useSend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| License | Apache 2.0 | AGPL-3.0 |
| Free tier (hosted) | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | 3,000 / mo, 100 / day |
| Paid pricing | Plans: $10 for 50k, $20 for 100k | Usage: $0.40 per 1k transactional, $1.00 per 1k marketing, $10 minimum |
| Sending path | Own MTA (KumoMTA) | Amazon SES |
| Self-host needs AWS | No | Yes (SES and SNS) |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | Not listed |
| REST API and SMTP | Yes | Yes |
| Webhooks | Yes, HMAC signed | Yes, HMAC signed |
| Contacts and campaigns | Yes | Yes |
| Event-triggered automations | Yes | Not listed |
| Inbound email | Mailboxes with threads, API, MCP, IMAP | On the roadmap |
| Status | Generally available | Beta, per the README |

## FAQ

### Is useSend the same as Unsend?

Yes. useSend is the current name of the project formerly called Unsend. The code lives at github.com/usesend/useSend.

### Do I need AWS to self-host Reloop?

No. Reloop runs its own mail server, so you need a server and DNS, not an AWS account. useSend's self-hosted setup requires Amazon SES and SNS.

### Which is cheaper?

On the hosted plans, Reloop is cheaper below about 250k emails a month and useSend is cheaper well above that for transactional mail. Self-hosted, Reloop has no per-email cost, while useSend passes through SES fees.

### Can useSend receive email?

Not yet. Inbound email is listed on its roadmap. Reloop receives mail into threaded mailboxes you can read over the API, MCP or IMAP.

### Which license is more permissive?

Reloop's Apache 2.0. useSend's AGPL-3.0 requires you to publish changes if you offer a modified version to others over a network.

# Reloop vs ZeptoMail

> Reloop vs ZeptoMail (now Zoho CPaaS) compared honestly: pay-as-you-go credits vs monthly plans, transactional-only rules, inbound and agent inboxes, campaigns, self-hosting, and how to switch.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/compare/zeptomail

Reloop vs ZeptoMail (now Zoho CPaaS) compared honestly: pay-as-you-go credits vs monthly plans, transactional-only rules, inbound and agent inboxes, campaigns, self-hosting, and how to switch.

Reloop is the email service / infrastructure (ESP + MTA). It is not a multi-ESP connector that sits on SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## Reloop vs ZeptoMail

| Feature | Reloop | ZeptoMail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pricing model | Monthly plans, or prepaid credits | Prepaid credits, no monthly fee |
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | First credit free (10,000 emails) |
| 50,000 emails | $10 / mo | About $12.50 in credits |
| 100,000 emails | $20 / mo | About $25 in credits |

## FAQ

### Is ZeptoMail cheaper than Reloop?

At high volume, yes. At the widely listed $2.50 per 10,000 emails, ZeptoMail is cheaper above roughly 150k emails a month. Below that, Reloop's $10 (50k) and $20 (100k) plans cost less.

### Can I send newsletters with ZeptoMail?

No. ZeptoMail's terms only allow transactional email and accounts that keep sending marketing mail get blocked. Reloop supports both transactional email and campaigns.

### What happened to ZeptoMail?

It's now part of Zoho CPaaS, which adds SMS, WhatsApp and voice to the same email infrastructure. The email API and SMTP relay still work the same way.

### Do ZeptoMail credits expire?

Yes, 6 months after purchase. Reloop's plans are monthly, with $0.50 per 1,000 emails above your plan's allowance.

### Can ZeptoMail receive email?

Its docs describe sending, templates and delivery webhooks, not inbound mailboxes. Reloop receives mail into threaded inboxes you can read over the API, MCP or IMAP.

# Reloop MCP server

Path: /features/mcp
URL: https://reloop.sh/features/mcp
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/features/mcp.md

# Reloop MCP server

> Connect any AI agent or MCP client to Reloop. It can do everything you can do in the Reloop dashboard.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/features/mcp
Server URL: https://reloop.sh/mcp
Connect from the dashboard: https://reloop.sh/dashboard/integrations/mcp
Docs: https://reloop.sh/docs/integrations/ai-tools/mcp-server

## How it works

1. **Add the server URL.** Paste the Reloop server URL into your client, or use its one-click install link.
2. **Sign in with Reloop.** Your client opens the browser. Sign in and approve the workspace. OAuth handles the token, so there is no API key to copy or rotate.
3. **Ask in plain language.** Ask for what you need. The agent picks the right Reloop tool, runs it against your workspace and tells you what happened.

## What it can do

- **Emails**: Send, batch, schedule and cancel email, and look up any message and its delivery status.
- **Contacts**: Add and update contacts, manage custom properties, segments and topic subscriptions.
- **Campaigns**: Draft a broadcast, pick the audience, schedule it or send it now.
- **Templates**: Create and edit reusable templates, such as a password reset that matches your brand.
- **Automation**: Build workflows that react to events, like a welcome series when someone signs up.
- **Inbox**: Read inbound email and attachments, and follow threads in your agent inboxes.
- **Metrics & logs**: Check delivery, bounce and open rates, and read the logs behind a change.
- **Domains**: Add a sending domain, get the DNS records and check verification.
- **Webhooks & API keys**: Create webhooks for delivery and inbound events, and manage API keys.

## Setup by client

- [Reloop MCP for Claude Code](https://reloop.sh/features/mcp/claude-code)
- [Reloop MCP for Claude](https://reloop.sh/features/mcp/claude)
- [Reloop MCP for Cursor](https://reloop.sh/features/mcp/cursor)
- [Reloop MCP for VS Code](https://reloop.sh/features/mcp/vscode)
- [Reloop MCP for Codex](https://reloop.sh/features/mcp/codex)

## Ask your agent to…

- Send a welcome email to user@example.com with a personalized greeting.
- List all emails I sent today and show their delivery status.
- Add a new contact with their name and email.
- Create a campaign for our product launch announcement.
- Verify my domain and check the DNS configuration status.
- Show me all inbound emails I received this week.
- Set up a webhook to notify me when an email bounces.
- Create a contact group for users who signed up this month.
- Send a batch of onboarding emails to these five new users.
- Create a password reset email template that matches our brand.
- Why did my bounce rate go up yesterday?
- Build an automation that sends a welcome series when someone signs up.

## Self-host and local (stdio)

Reloop is open source. Remote clients can use the /mcp endpoint of your own install. Clients that only launch local servers can run reloop-mcp with an API key:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "reloop": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "reloop-mcp"
      ],
      "env": {
        "RELOOP_API_KEY": "YOUR_API_KEY",
        "RELOOP_BASE_URL": "https://mail.example.com"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## FAQ

### What is the Reloop MCP server?

A Model Context Protocol server at https://reloop.sh/mcp that connects AI clients to your Reloop workspace. It can do everything you can do in the Reloop dashboard: send email, manage contacts, run campaigns, edit templates, build automations, read the inbox, check metrics and logs, verify domains, and manage webhooks and API keys.

### Do I need an API key?

Not for the hosted server. Your client signs in with Reloop over OAuth: the browser opens, you approve the workspace, and the client receives a token scoped to it. API keys are only needed when you run reloop-mcp locally over stdio.

### Which AI clients work with it?

Claude Code, Claude (web and desktop), Cursor, VS Code with GitHub Copilot agent mode, and Codex have setup guides. Any client that supports remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP can connect with the server URL, and clients that only launch local servers can run reloop-mcp over stdio.

### Can I use it with a self-hosted Reloop install?

Yes. Reloop is open source. Point remote clients at the /mcp endpoint of your own install, or run npx -y reloop-mcp with RELOOP_API_KEY set to a key from your install and RELOOP_BASE_URL set to its public URL.

### Should I use the MCP server or the CLI?

Use the MCP server in chat and IDE clients that support MCP, where you ask in plain language. Use the Reloop CLI in shells, CI jobs and agents that run commands: every command takes --json and returns predictable exit codes.

# Reloop CLI

Path: /features/cli
URL: https://reloop.sh/features/cli
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/features/cli.md

# Reloop CLI

> Send, schedule and receive email from your terminal, CI or a coding agent. Every command supports --json.

HTML: https://reloop.sh/features/cli
Docs: https://reloop.sh/docs/integrations/ai-tools/cli-agents

## Install and sign in

```bash
npx -y reloop-cli init --all --browser
```

## Agent skill

```bash
npx skills add reloop/reloop-cli
```

## Send an email

```bash
reloop emails send \
  --from "you@yourdomain.com" \
  --to "user@example.com" \
  --subject "Hello from Reloop" \
  --text "It works."
```

## JSON output for agents

Add --json to any command. Output goes to stdout with no spinners, exit codes are 0 for success and 1 for errors, and every error has a message and a code.

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "No API key found",
    "code": "auth_error"
  }
}
```

## Pipe content from stdin

Pass - to any file flag to read from stdin. Works with --text-file, --html-file and --file.

```bash
echo "Your order has shipped." | reloop emails send \
  --from "Acme <onboarding@example.com>" \
  --to delivered@example.com \
  --subject "Order update" \
  --text-file -
```

## Batch sending

Send up to 100 emails in one request from a JSON file or a pipe.

```bash
cat emails.json | reloop emails batch --file -
```

## Safe retries

Retry a failed send with the same --idempotency-key and Reloop won't deliver it twice. Supported on emails send and emails batch.

```bash
reloop emails send \
  --from "Acme <onboarding@example.com>" \
  --to delivered@example.com \
  --subject "Welcome" \
  --text "Hello!" \
  --idempotency-key "welcome-user-123"
```

## Scheduling

Schedule with --scheduled-at, then cancel or reschedule by id.

```bash
reloop emails send \
  --from "Acme <onboarding@example.com>" \
  --to delivered@example.com \
  --subject "Your trial ends soon" \
  --text "Your free trial expires in 3 days." \
  --scheduled-at "tomorrow at 9am ET"

reloop emails cancel <id>
reloop emails update <id> --scheduled-at <datetime>
```

## Read inbound email

Stream new inbound email as JSON from a long-running process, or fetch one by id. Needs a verified domain with receiving enabled.

```bash
reloop emails receiving listen --json

reloop emails receiving get <email-id>
```

## Webhooks in your terminal

Subscribe to webhook events and stream them to your terminal, or forward them to a local server. The webhook is removed when you disconnect.

```bash
reloop webhooks listen \
  --url https://hostname.tailnet-name.ts.net \
  --events email.delivered email.bounced email.received

reloop webhooks listen \
  --url https://hostname.tailnet-name.ts.net \
  --forward-to http://localhost:4321/api/webhook
```

## FAQ

### How do I install the Reloop CLI?

Run npx -y reloop-cli init --all --browser. It sets up the CLI and opens your browser so you can authorize your workspace.

### How do AI agents use the CLI?

Install the agent skill with npx skills add reloop/reloop-cli so Claude Code, Codex and other skill-aware agents know the commands. Agents pass --json to get machine-readable output, exit code 0 on success and 1 on errors, and errors with a message and a code.

### Can I send email in bulk?

Yes. reloop emails batch sends up to 100 emails in a single request. Pass a JSON file, or use --file - to read it from stdin.

### How do I avoid duplicate sends when retrying?

Pass --idempotency-key with a stable value, such as welcome-user-123. Retrying with the same key won't send the email again. It works on emails send and emails batch.

### Can the CLI receive email?

Yes. reloop emails receiving listen --json streams new inbound email, and reloop emails receiving get fetches one by id. You need a verified domain with receiving enabled.

### How do I test webhooks locally?

Run reloop webhooks listen with a public --url (Tailscale Funnel, ngrok or similar) and the events you want. Add --forward-to to send them to a local server. The webhook is removed when you press Ctrl+C.

# Reloop

Path: /
URL: https://reloop.sh
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/index.md

# Reloop

> High-performance, open-source email infrastructure: the same service as proprietary platforms. Use Reloop hosted or deploy it yourself.

Reloop is email infrastructure for developers: transactional and marketing email, real-time webhooks, inbound processing, analytics, and an agent-ready API. Reloop **is** the ESP; it runs an in-house MTA (KumoMTA), not a connector that routes through SendGrid, Mailgun, Resend, or SES.

## What Reloop is not

- Not a multi-provider email router
- Not MIT-licensed (Apache 2.0 with Reloop Labs use restrictions)
- Not a contact-list ESP (Reloop Cloud bills by emails sent)
- Self-host is not a paid Reloop Cloud SKU

## Who it is for

Developers, startups, and agent products that need transactional + campaign email, optional self-host, and machine-readable docs.

## Hosted pricing (Reloop Cloud)

Canonical data: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md

- Free: $0, 6,000 emails / month, **200 / day**
- Pro: $10 / month, 50,000 emails / month, no daily cap, overage $0.50 / 1,000
- Growth: $20 / month, 100,000 emails / month, no daily cap, overage $0.50 / 1,000
- Enterprise: custom volume and billing

## Why Reloop

- **Open source**: same product you can self-host or use hosted (Apache 2.0)
- **Developer-first**: REST API, SMTP relay, official SDKs, CLI, MCP
- **Agent-ready**: API keys, inbound agent inbox, docs as markdown / llms.txt

## Get started

- Hosted signup: https://reloop.sh/dashboard/signup
- Pricing: https://reloop.sh/pricing.md
- Documentation index: https://reloop.sh/llms-docs.txt

# About Reloop

Reloop Labs builds open-source email infrastructure for developers and AI agents. Reloop **is** the email platform (ESP + MTA). It is **not** a multi-ESP connector.

## What we build

- Hosted Reloop Cloud (email API and SMTP) at reloop.sh
- Self-hostable Apache License 2.0 stack plus Reloop Labs additional restrictions: personal and internal use allowed; no commercial redistribution, hosted services, or competing products. No Reloop license fee; you pay your infra. See https://reloop.sh/license
- Agent skills, MCP server, and agent-friendly documentation

## Who it is for

Solo developers, startups, and teams that want transactional + marketing email without lock-in, plus inbound email for agents.

## What Reloop is not

- Not MIT-licensed
- Not a SendGrid/Mailgun/Resend/SES proxy
- Not priced by stored contacts on Reloop Cloud

# Reloop vs MailerSend (2026): Pricing, Features and Which to Choose

Path: /blog/reloop-vs-mailersend
URL: https://reloop.sh/blog/reloop-vs-mailersend
Markdown: https://reloop.sh/blog/reloop-vs-mailersend.md

Reloop vs MailerSend compared: pricing from 500 to 500k emails a month, API and SDKs, inbound email, templates, dedicated IPs, self-hosting, and how to switch.

**MailerSend and Reloop are both developer-first transactional email APIs, and both send from code in a few lines.** The differences are price, scope and control: **Reloop costs $10 for 50k emails where MailerSend's Starter plan is $35, stores inbound mail in real inboxes instead of forwarding it, and is open source, so you can run it yourself.** MailerSend has the more polished no-code side: a drag-and-drop builder, SMS, email verification and split testing.

We build Reloop, so read this with that in mind. MailerSend's numbers come from its public [pricing page](https://www.mailersend.com/pricing) and [API docs](https://developers.mailersend.com), checked in October 2026. Where MailerSend is the better pick, we say so.

---

## The 30-second comparison

| | **Reloop** | **MailerSend** |
|---|---|---|
| Free tier | 6,000 / mo, 200 / day | 500 / mo, 100 API requests / day |
| 50,000 emails / mo | **$10** | $35 (Starter) |
| 100,000 emails / mo | **$20** | $68 (Starter) |
| Overage per 1,000 | **$0.50** | $1.30 at the 50k and 100k tiers |
| Dedicated IP | Included on Growth ($20) | Add-on on Professional |
| Open source | Yes (Apache 2.0) | No |
| Self-host | Yes | No |
| Inbound email | Mailboxes with threads, API, MCP, IMAP | Parsed and forwarded to a webhook or address |
| Agent inbox | Yes | No |
| Contacts, campaigns, automations | Yes | Bulk sending; marketing lives in MailerLite |
| Drag-and-drop builder | No | Yes |
| SMS | No | Yes (US and Canada) |
| SMTP relay | Yes | Yes |

MailerSend prices above are monthly billing; annual billing takes 10% off. Reloop's prices are on [reloop.sh/pricing](/pricing). Both change, so check before you commit.

---

## Pricing at real volumes

MailerSend's free plan is small: 500 emails a month, 1 domain, 1 template, 1 webhook and 100 API requests a day. Reloop's free tier sends 6,000 a month with a 200-a-day cap. If you're past testing, MailerSend's Hobby plan is $7 a month for 5,000 emails.

From there, the gap grows with volume:

| Monthly volume | Reloop | MailerSend Starter | Difference per year |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3,000 | $0 | $7 (Hobby) | $84 |
| 50,000 | $10 | $35 | $300 |
| 100,000 | $20 | $68 | **$576** |
| 250,000 | $20 + $75 overage = $95 | $162.50 | $810 |
| 500,000 | $20 + $200 overage = $220 | $325 | $1,260 |

MailerSend's Professional plan, which adds unlimited domains, users and templates, 30-day activity retention and the dedicated IP add-on, is $110 for 50k and $140 for 100k.

Two things drive the difference:

- **Reloop's paid plans start lower.** $10 for 50k and $20 for 100k, with a dedicated IP included at $20.
- **Overage is cheaper.** Extra mail on Reloop is $0.50 per 1,000. On MailerSend Starter it's $1.30 per 1,000 at the 50k and 100k tiers.

If you self-host Reloop, there's no per-email fee at all. You pay for the server. See [self-hosted email infrastructure](/blog/self-hosted-email-infrastructure) for what that really involves.

<Callout type="tip">
  Price the volume you expect in a year, not today's. Switching providers later means new DNS records and warming reputation again, so pick one that still makes sense at 10× your current volume.
</Callout>

---

## Developer experience

Both APIs are clean REST with official SDKs. MailerSend uses a builder pattern; Reloop takes a plain object.

**MailerSend**

```typescript

const mailerSend = new MailerSend({ apiKey: process.env.MAILERSEND_API_KEY! });

const emailParams = new EmailParams()
  .setFrom(new Sender("hello@acme.com", "Acme"))
  .setTo([new Recipient("user@example.com", "User")])
  .setSubject("Welcome")
  .setHtml("<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>");

await mailerSend.email.send(emailParams);
```

**Reloop**

```typescript

const reloop = new Reloop({ apiKey: process.env.RELOOP_API_KEY! });

const { response, emailError } = await reloop.mail.send({
  from: "Acme <hello@mail.acme.com>",
  to: "user@example.com",
  subject: "Welcome",
  html: "<p>Thanks for signing up.</p>",
});
```

Reloop returns errors as values instead of throwing. Other differences:

| | Reloop | MailerSend |
|---|---|---|
| Request style | Plain object | Builder (`EmailParams`, `Sender`, `Recipient`) |
| Error format | `message`, `why` and `fix` | `message` and `errors` |
| Template variables | `{{{first_name}}}` | `{{first_name}}` (personalization) |
| Recipients per email | `to`, `cc`, `bcc` | Up to 50 |
| Webhook signature | `Reloop-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256) | `Signature` (HMAC-SHA256) |
| Event names | `email.delivered`, `email.bounced`, … | `activity.delivered`, `activity.hard_bounced`, … |

Reloop's error shape is the one strong opinion here. When a send fails, the error says **why** and **how to fix it**:

```json
{
  "message": "Domain not found",
  "why": "The domain mail.acme.com was not found or is not authorized for your organization",
  "fix": "Ensure the domain is registered and verified in your dashboard"
}
```

MailerSend's docs are thorough and it ships SDKs for seven languages plus an OpenAPI collection, so you won't be short of examples.

---

## Receiving email and agent inboxes

**MailerSend** has inbound routing on its paid plans. Incoming mail is parsed and forwarded as JSON to your webhook, or forwarded to another address, with rules by recipient, domain or header. MailerSend doesn't store it as a mailbox, and each forward counts against your monthly email quota.

**Reloop** receives mail into **mailboxes**. Messages are stored, threaded, spam-scored with Rspamd, and readable over the API, the [MCP server](/docs/integrations/ai-tools/mcp-server) or IMAP. You can reply in-thread with one call, and there's an `email.received` webhook if you want push notifications too.

That matters if you're building:

- **AI agents that handle email.** Give an agent its own address, let it read the thread and reply. See [build an AI agent that reads and replies to email](/blog/build-ai-agent-sends-emails).
- **Support or shared inboxes** where humans and agents work the same threads.
- **Reply handling** for transactional mail ("reply to this email to comment").

| | Reloop | MailerSend |
|---|---|---|
| Receive on your domain | Yes | Yes (paid plans) |
| Stored mailboxes with threads | Yes | No |
| Reply in thread via API | Yes | Build it yourself |
| IMAP access | Yes | No |

---

## Templates, marketing and automations

MailerSend is strong on the visual side. It has a drag-and-drop builder, a rich-text editor, an HTML editor, and split testing. Non-developers can build and edit templates without touching code.

Reloop's templates are code-first: store HTML or a React Email component, send it by ID, and fill in `{{{variables}}}`. There's no drag-and-drop builder today.

On marketing, MailerSend focuses on transactional mail and points marketing teams to its sister product, MailerLite. Reloop has it in one place: contacts with custom properties, groups, subscription channels, scheduled broadcast campaigns, and **event-triggered automations** with delays, conditions and email steps. See [welcome sequences that convert](/blog/welcome-email-sequences-that-convert) for a worked example.

---

## Deliverability

Deliverability comes down mostly to your domain setup and list hygiene. Both handle SPF, DKIM and DMARC setup, bounce and complaint events, open and click tracking, and suppression lists.

The differences:

- **Dedicated IPs.** Reloop includes one on Growth ($20/mo). MailerSend offers a dedicated IP add-on on Professional, recommended for more than 100k emails a week.
- **Monitoring.** MailerSend includes DMARC monitoring and blocklist monitoring on Starter and Professional. Reloop ships free [domain reputation](/tools/domain-reputation-checker), [blocklist](/tools/blocklist-checker) and [auth](/tools/auth-checker) checkers.
- **Sending path.** Reloop runs its own MTA (KumoMTA) with per-domain throttling and automatic pauses when bounce or complaint rates spike. Read [how bounce processing works](/blog/email-bounce-processing-automation).

---

## Self-hosting and lock-in

MailerSend is hosted-only. Your templates, logs and suppression lists live in its database, and activity data is kept for 1 to 30 days depending on plan (longer is a paid add-on).

Reloop is Apache 2.0. You can:

1. Start on Reloop Cloud.
2. Move to your own server later with the [one-command installer](/self-host) or [Coolify](/blog/reloop-coolify-setup).
3. Keep the same API. Point the SDK's `baseUrl` at your instance and nothing else in your code changes.

That helps with data residency, security reviews that need to read the code handling your users' mail, and insurance against price changes. Self-hosting does mean you own IP reputation, warm-up and uptime, so most teams start hosted.

---

## Where MailerSend is the better choice

- **Non-developers edit your emails.** The drag-and-drop builder and template editors are more complete than anything Reloop offers.
- **You need SMS** alongside email, or built-in email verification and split testing, from one vendor.
- **You already use MailerLite** for marketing and want the sister product for transactional mail.

Comparing more providers? See our roundup of the [best MailerSend alternatives](/blog/best-mailersend-alternatives).

## Where Reloop is the better choice

- **Cost matters past a few thousand emails.** $10 vs $35 at 50k, $20 vs $68 at 100k.
- **You need inbound mail as real inboxes**, especially for AI agents.
- **You want transactional mail, campaigns and automations** in one product with one suppression list.
- **You need open source or self-hosting.**

---

## Switching from MailerSend to Reloop

1. **Add your domain in Reloop** and publish the DKIM record (`reloop._domainkey`). Merge `include:reloop.sh` into your existing SPF record rather than adding a second one.
2. **Swap the client.** Replace the `EmailParams` builder and `mailerSend.email.send` with a single `reloop.mail.send` call.
3. **Move templates.** Change personalization placeholders to triple braces: `{{first_name}}` becomes `{{{first_name}}}`.
4. **Export your suppression list** from MailerSend and import it into Reloop, so you never mail an address that bounced or complained.
5. **Point webhooks** at a new handler. Map `activity.delivered` → `email.delivered`, `activity.hard_bounced` → `email.bounced`, `activity.spam_complaint` → `email.complained`, and verify the `Reloop-Signature` header instead of `Signature`.
6. **Move inbound routes** to a Reloop mailbox, or keep using a webhook with `email.received`.
7. **Ramp traffic** from 10% to 100% over a week or two, then remove MailerSend's DNS records.

Our [SendGrid migration guide](/blog/migrating-from-sendgrid) walks through the traffic split and suppression import in more detail; the same steps work from MailerSend.

---
